citation.authors: Nwachukwu DC, Aneke E, Nwachukwu NZ, Obika LF et al

cited_by.title: Hibiscus (sorrel, zobo, bissap) and blood pressure

record.population: 80 newly diagnosed, untreated Nigerian adults with mild to moderate hypertension, Enugu
record.design: Randomised, three groups for 4 weeks: placebo, hydrochlorothiazide, or hibiscus
record.finding: Both hibiscus and the drug lowered blood pressure compared with placebo. The authors reported hibiscus as more effective than the drug and without electrolyte imbalance, and the fall persisted after withdrawal. No side effects were reported.
record.note: Single small trial. Placebo, dose and blinding details were not in the abstract. The 'more effective than the drug' conclusion is the authors' own.
